Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Sarah Smith, DOB: 20/04/1983, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded, Practice: Not recorded, Practice Address: Not recorded, Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Stress-related anxiety symptoms/postpartum anxiety with palpitations and tachycardia  
- Secondary: Differential diagnosis of pulmonary embolism (medical emergency) strongly suspected  
- Tertiary: Possible respiratory infection (bronchitis/pneumonia) and post-surgical pain contributing to symptoms

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented; used regularly post-C-section but stopped approx. 1 week ago)  
- Allergies/ADRs: Allergy to Ibuprofen, reaction not specified  
- Past Medical History: No chronic illnesses reported  

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded  
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded  
- Family History: Mother has history of venous thromboembolism (clots in legs)  

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives at home alone with baby; partner currently at work  
- Social Support: Partner present but at work; no other support mentioned  
- Occupation/Education: Not recorded  
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded  
- Smoking/Substance Use: Not recorded  
- Key Stressors: Newborn care postpartum; recent C-section (4 weeks ago); acute physical symptoms causing distress  

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded  
- Mood & Affect: Patient reports feeling “really stressed out” due to symptoms  
- Speech & Thought: Speech normal, coherent; thoughts relevant, no psychosis noted  
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported  

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded  
- Attention/Concentration: Not recorded  
- Memory: Not recorded  
- Insight & Judgement: Patient demonstrates understanding of symptoms and agrees to follow urgent medical advice  

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded  
- Appetite: Not recorded  
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded  
- Anxiety Symptoms: Feeling stressed, palpitations, tachycardia (~180 bpm), increased heart awareness  

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Not recorded; no indications from transcript  
- Protective Factors: Understanding of symptoms and willingness to seek urgent medical care  
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Moderate, due to acute physical symptoms and stress; medically prioritized for potential life-threatening condition  
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded  

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Recent major surgery (C-section), family history of venous thromboembolism, postpartum physiological stress  
- Precipitating factors: Sudden onset shortness of breath, palpitations, chest soreness, recent cough  
- Perpetuating factors: Anxiety about health, ongoing baby care responsibilities with limited immediate social support  
- Protective factors: Patient insight, willingness to seek hospital care promptly

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Stress-related anxiety symptoms/postpartum anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce feelings of stress and anxiety related to physical symptoms and postpartum adjustments  
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide reassurance; monitor anxiety symptoms; support coping strategies and connect with appropriate mental health resources postpartum  
- Actions (Patient): Engage in relaxation techniques; attend follow-up mental health review; communicate any worsening anxiety or new symptoms  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide psychoeducation on anxiety and postpartum adjustment; screen for persistent anxiety symptoms on follow-up; consider referral to perinatal mental health services if indicated  

Secondary Problem: Pulmonary embolism (medical emergency)
- Patient Goal(s): To safely access emergency medical evaluation and treatment promptly  
- Clinical Goal(s): Ensure immediate assessment and management of suspected pulmonary embolism  
- Actions (Patient): Proceed to hospital emergency department promptly with baby as advised; avoid analgesics like codeine until assessment  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Urgent recommendation for hospital evaluation; arrange ambulance if patient deteriorates; monitor clinical status via follow-up call  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Recognition of symptom severity prompting urgent care; potential risks of post-C-section thromboembolism; anxiety and stress management postpartum  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or worsening anxiety symptoms  
- Coping Strategies: Stress reduction techniques, paced breathing, rest, seeking social support  

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Implied from agreement to proceed to hospital; explicit documentation not recorded  
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable  
- Review Date: Not recorded; advised urgent physical health follow-up and recommend mental health review postpartum  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Pulmonary Embolism: High likelihood. Supported by recent C-section, sudden onset dyspnea, tachycardia, chest soreness, family history of clots. Requires urgent exclusion.  
- Respiratory Infection (Bronchitis/Pneumonia): Medium likelihood. New cough and chest soreness may indicate infection but less typical for sudden symptoms without fever.  
- Postpartum Anxiety/Panic Attack: Medium likelihood. Stress and palpitations present; anxiety may contribute but organic causes must be excluded first.  

Quality checks  
● Missing but clinically expected elements: MSE details, risk assessment of suicidal ideation, formal cognitive examination, follow-up plan for mental health symptoms  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted; DDx supports clinical impression consistent with transcript  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear; information comprehensive though focused on presenting physical symptoms with incidental anxiety symptoms mentioned
